summary: James Wilkinson Breeks (1830–1872) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (~1850–1852) and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1852 to 1872.

James Wilson (1853–1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1870–1874) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1874–1875), and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1873 to 1910.

Linguist James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) studied at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell University (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab.

The 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge (1954–1992) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche (1973), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo (~1833–1853), and taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.

Jamie Hubbard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. At Smith College, he held the Yehan Numata and Conway professorships (attested 2016, emeritus 2026).
Jampa Lhundup works in Tibetology and linguistics. Attested in 2026, he studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as an assistant professor of art history and served on its faculty.

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa from Sera Monastery (-1958) and degrees at the University of Munich (~1968–1979), later working at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1982–2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987) and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as director (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2015, 2026).

Jampal Kunzang Rechung (born 1930) is a Tibetology scholar. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988) and deputy director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (1912–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo, studied under masters such as Khenpo Thupten and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught students including Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a master of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, and taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Indologist Jan A. Schoterman (1948–1989) earned degrees including a PhD from Utrecht University (1968–1982) under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1982–1989), Tilburg University, and the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (~1983–1989).

Jan Brunson works in Indology and other fields. She earned a PhD from Brown University (-2008) and held posts as Visiting Assistant Professor at Bowdoin College (2008–2011) and Affiliate Faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2011).

Jan C. Heesterman (1925–2014) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1953–1957). He succeeded F. B. J. Kuiper in 1972 and served as professor at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990.

Jan Chozen Bays (born 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Swarthmore College and UC San Diego, she studied Zen under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, founded Heart of Wisdom Zen Temple, and became abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery (~2002).
